subject: SLA template: uptime & latency commitments + monthly credit cap request
messages:
From: Elena Sokolov <elena.sokolov@finedge.io>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finedge.io
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA template: uptime, latency & monthly credits — request for exceptions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers look strong. Before we sign, our procurement and engineering teams asked us to propose a small set of deviations to Redwood's standard SLA template so we can align internal budgeting and incident handling. High-level asks: 

- Standard uptime: we'd like 99.95% for the Core Inference API (not just embeddings). Can Redwood commit to that as a baseline?
- Latency: we need a 95th percentile <= 250ms for small prompt sizes during business hours (US-EAST). If that can't be guaranteed, we'd like explicit language and a narrower credit band.
- Monthly service credits: procurement prefers a hard cap at 25% of monthly spend and a carveout for scheduled maintenance with 72-hour advance notice.

Can you share a marked-up SLA that shows where Redwood can accept these and where you need standard carveouts? We want to get to signature + PO issuance (PO 12345) by next Thursday if possible.

Attachment: FinEdge-PO-12345.pdf (PDF stub)

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Sokolov
Head of Platform Operations, FinEdge
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Sokolov <elena.sokolov@finedge.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime, latency & monthly credits — request for exceptions

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks and the PO. Looping in Ben (AE) and Laura (Legal) so we can get the contract redlines reviewed quickly. Preliminary thoughts:

- 99.95% uptime for Core API: possible for dedicated tiers; on hosted plans we'd need to verify capacity commitments and may propose a mixed baseline (99.9% hosted / 99.95% dedicated).
- Latency 95p <= 250ms: engineering needs to confirm for the exact prompt distribution you expect. We can scope through an agreed benchmark prompt set as part of the SLA appendix.
- Monthly credit cap at 25%: Laura and finance need to confirm, but we typically agree to a monthly cap in the 15–30% range depending on the commitment level.

We will prepare a marked-up SLA and a credit matrix for your review by tomorrow EOD. Ben — can you confirm the commitment tier FinEdge is intending to purchase so we can match the numbers to the right offering?

Thanks,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Sokolov <elena.sokolov@finedge.io>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime, latency & monthly credits — request for exceptions

Elena —

Thanks for the PO and the clarity. FinEdge is listed in our renewal pipeline as a Reserved (dedicated) deployment, correct? If so, here's a proposal we feel is reasonable and maps to the Dedicated offering: 

Proposed adjustments (summary):
- Uptime: 99.95% monthly for Core Inference API (applies to dedicated pool only).
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 250ms for prompt set A (business hours 8am–8pm ET). We'll include an appendix with your benchmark prompt set to be recorded at go-live.
- Monthly service credit matrix (examples):
  - 99.95%–100%: 0% credit
  - 99.8%–99.949%: 5% credit
  - 99.0%–99.799%: 15% credit
  - <99.0%: 25% credit (monthly cap)
- Maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance with >72 hours notice is excluded; emergency maintenance requires notice as soon as practicable.
- Claims window: customer must file for credit within 30 days of the incident month.
- Cap: total credits per month capped at 25% of that month's invoice.

I've attached a draft credit matrix and a redline on the SLA template for you to review. If these numbers work, Laura and I can lock them in and then send a DocuSign for signatures.

Attachment: SLA_credit_matrix_v3.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 12KB)
Attachment: Redwood-SLA-draft-20261018.pdf (PDF redline)

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Sokolov <elena.sokolov@finedge.io>, ben_carter@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T12:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime, latency & monthly credits — request for exceptions

Elena —

Thanks for the edits. A couple of legal points we propose as small clarifications/redlines before signature: 

1) Claims timing: we are comfortable with a 30-day claims window (Ben's suggestion) but would like explicit language that credits are calculated only against fees actually paid in the month the outage(s) occurred.
2) Maintenance definition: scheduled maintenance must be posted on the account portal and provided in writing 72 hours prior; emergency maintenance to include an incident summary within 5 business days.
3) Liability cap: we prefer a single aggregate liability cap equal to the total fees paid in the prior 12 months. If FinEdge requests a higher cap, we'd need C-level approval.

Minor ask for procurement: please confirm whether the PO (12345) will reference the Redwood master services schedule or whether you require a signed attachment as the operative SLA. If you need the SLA embedded into the PO itself, we may need a short turnaround to prepare the correct DocuSign envelope.

On the credit cap: 25% is within reason for a dedicated commitment. Please confirm the commitment level (monthly committed spend) so we can finalize the numbers.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Sokolov <elena.sokolov@finedge.io>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime, latency & monthly credit cap request

Hi team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the detailed matrix. A few quick notes from procurement and engineering here: 

- FinEdge confirms this will be a dedicated deployment with an initial committed monthly spend of ~$95k (so 25% cap is within our threshold).
- Procurement: PO 12345 will reference the Redwood Master Services Schedule; please include the signed SLA as an attachment in the DocuSign envelope.
- Engineering: we'll provide the benchmark prompt set A by EOD tomorrow so you can validate the 95p latency target.

If you can produce a DocuSign with the redlined SLA and the credit matrix attached, we'll aim to review and sign within 48 hours.

Attachment: FinEdge-PO-12345.pdf (PDF stub)

Thanks — looking forward to closing.
Elena
Elena Sokolov
Head of Platform Operations, FinEdge
